# Hermes Agent FAQ & Troubleshooting Guide

## 1. Getting Started, UI & Observability
- **Web Dashboard:** Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web interface on `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, which includes an embedded browser chat.
- **Observability / Tracing:** Langfuse is bundled as an opt-in plugin. Run `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse` (or use `hermes tools`) to view full execution traces and inspect tool input/output parameter chains.
- **Reporting Vulnerabilities:** Follow `SECURITY.md`. Report via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or email `security@nousresearch.com`.

---

## 2. Model Providers & Authentication
- **Local Ollama Overridden by Env Keys:** If `base_url: http://localhost:11434` triggers remote 401 errors, your environment has remote keys set (e.g., Anthropic). Set `provider: custom` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to disable automatic provider routing.
- **Ollama Cloud 404s:** Ollama Cloud uses OpenAI-compatible `/v1` routes (`https://ollama.com/v1`). Set `provider: ollama-cloud` to avoid legacy `/api` route 404s.
- **Small Local Models (4B–9B) Run Slowly:** Hermes injects the full tool schema (~45 tools) on each turn. For better throughput:
  1. Disable unused toolsets via `hermes tools`.
  2. Use faster quantization or larger models (32B+).
  3. Set `terminal.backend: local` to bypass container overhead.
- **Custom / Local Vision:** Add `supports_vision: true` to your custom model config to pass native image payloads.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` or set `provider: azure-foundry` (auto-detects `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`). Claude Code variables (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) are ignored.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs. API Mode:** Anthropic API keys always incur API token costs. To use Pro/Max subscription allowances, authenticate via OAuth.
- **Google Gemini:** `google-gemini-cli` OAuth has been deprecated due to upstream bans. Authenticate using `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` with Google AI Studio.
- **DeepSeek V4 Model Aliasing:** If `deepseek-v4-flash` maps to `deepseek-chat` / pro pricing, update to current `main` to ensure flash models pass through without normalization.
- **LocalAI / OpenAI Usage Metrics:** OpenAI-compatible streaming automatically forwards `stream_options: {include_usage: true}` to populate token counters in `/usage`.

---

## 3. Context, Memory & Personas
- **Agent Identity Files:**
  - `SOUL.md`: Base agent persona and behavioral instructions.
  - `USER.md`: Persistent user identity, profile, and preferences (`target="user"`).
  - `MEMORY.md`: General knowledge and recalled facts.
- **Tool Limits & Autonomous Runs:** The per-session turn limit is controlled by `agent.max_turns` (default: 90; CLI override: `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`). For long-running, persistent tasks across sessions, use `/goal` (Ralph loop) and resume with `/goal resume`.
- **Context Management:** `ContextCompressor` automatically prunes and deduplicates stale tool outputs. Alternative strategies can be set via `context.engine`.
- **Skill Usage Tracking:** View execution frequency and timestamps via `/insights` or `hermes insights` (backed by `~/.hermes/skills/.usage.json`).

---

## 4. Gateway & Messaging Integrations
- **Interactive Setup:** Configure messaging platforms (Discord, Telegram, etc.) interactively with `hermes gateway setup`.
- **Telegram "Unauthorized User" Fix:** `allowed_chats` only filters group IDs. For direct messages:
  - Add your numeric ID to `telegram.allow_from` (sets `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`).
  - DM the bot, then approve the code on the host: `hermes pairing approve telegram <CODE>`.
  - Or set `telegram.allow_all: true`.
- **Channel Personas:** Define per-room/group prompts across Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost via `channel_prompts`.
- **Multiplexing Profiles:** Run multiple isolated accounts (e.g., distinct WeChat/Telegram profiles) concurrently under a single gateway instance.
- **File & Media Delivery:** Outbound files dispatch to Matrix (`m.file`), Telegram, and Email (SMTP attachments). Remote Markdown images (`![image](url)`) are supported on DingTalk. MCP image outputs (`MEDIA:<path>`) forward automatically to supported platforms.
- **Inbound Attachments:** Uploaded text and code files (`.py`, `.txt`) are automatically injected into context.
- **Session Continuity:** Sessions interrupted by restarts default to `resume_pending` rather than being cleared; automatic idle reset is disabled by default (`session_reset.mode: none`).

---

## 5. Extensibility & Development
- **Smart Model Routing:** Automatic per-turn/cost-tier model routing is not supported by design. Use `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` for subagents, or switch manually via `/model`.
- **Subagents:** Launch concurrent subagent workers (default: up to 3) using `delegate_task`.
- **Custom Tools:** Create personal tools as standalone plugins inside `~/.hermes/plugins/` and activate with `hermes plugins enable <name>`. Core development requires definitions in `tools/` and registration in `toolsets.py`.
- **Custom Memory Providers:** In-tree additions to `plugins/memory/` are closed. Distribute external backends as plugins implementing the `MemoryProvider` ABC (`sync_turn`, `prefetch`, `shutdown`).

---

## 6. Installation & Platform Notes
- **Windows 10/11:** Tier 1 native support via PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). WSL2 is only required if using the Dashboard POSIX PTY `/chat` terminal pane.
- **Docker / NAS Permissions:** Map container user permissions on UGOS/Synology/unRAID using `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) to prevent `[Errno 13] Permission denied` on `/opt/data`. Multi-arch images support `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` (Apple Silicon / Raspberry Pi).
- **Android / Termux:** Supported out-of-the-box via `scripts/install.sh` using the `.[termux-all]` dependency set.
- **Local Honcho:** Setting `base_url` to `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` automatically injects placeholder credentials—no remote API key required.
- **Slow Updates:** Pauses during `hermes update` at the Node.js step are typically Camofox silently downloading browser binaries.
